KEYWORDS: 1-800-GOT-JUNK couch removal cost, sofa removal price, junk removal pricing, single item junk removal, 1800 got junk couch price 

# 1‑800‑GOT‑JUNK Couch and Sofa Removal Cost – The Complete Guide 

**A single couch or sofa from 1‑800‑GOT‑JUNK costs between **$59 and $170**.** The final number is given after a free on‑site estimate, because the price varies with your zip code, the couch’s size and weight, and local disposal fees. 

Below you’ll find exactly how that range is calculated, when a solo pickup is worth it, how to prepare the item, cheaper alternatives, and a side‑by‑side price comparison with the main competitors.

--- 

## How 1‑800‑GOT‑JUNK Prices Couch Removal 

### Volume vs. Single‑Item Pricing 

1‑800‑GOT‑JUNK primarily uses a **volume‑based pricing model** measured in 1/8‑truck increments. A “minimum load” (1/8 truck) is **$100‑$150**. If your couch fits inside that tiny space, the crew will quote you the minimum‑load price *plus* any applicable per‑item surcharge. 

When a customer requests **only one item**, the company also publishes a “single‑item removal” range of **$70‑$400**. Within that range, a couch typically lands between **$59‑$170**—the lower end reflecting a lightweight loveseat in a low‑cost market, the higher end reflecting a large sectional in a high‑cost metro. 

### What the $59‑$170 Range Means 

| Factor | Low‑End Impact | High‑End Impact |
|--------|----------------|-----------------|
| **Zip code / market** | Rural or low‑cost landfill fees | NYC, SF, Boston, Seattle |
| **Couch size & weight** | Loveseat, light fabric, <150 lb | Large sectional, leather, >250 lb |
| **Local disposal regulations** | No extra recycling fees | State‑mandated mattress fee ($10.50) if a mattress is attached |
| **Truck load** | Fits in 1/8‑truck (1.25 ft × 5 ft × 8 ft) | Requires half‑truck (5 ft × 5 ft × 8 ft) |

Because the crew measures the actual volume on the day, the **on‑site estimate** is the only way to lock in a precise number.

--- 

## What’s Included in the Quote 

### Labor, Loading, Hauling, Disposal, Cleanup 

* **All labor** – the crew does the heavy lifting; you never have to move the couch to the curb. 
* **Loading from anywhere on the property** – stairs, basements, garages are covered. 
* **Hauling and disposal** – the truck takes the couch to an authorized landfill or recycling center; any disposal fees are baked into the price. 
* **Cleanup** – the crew sweeps the area after loading. 

### Fees and Regulations 

* **Mattress recycling fee** – In California, Connecticut and Rhode Island, a **$10.50** per‑unit fee is mandated by the “Bye Bye Mattress” program (2026). 1‑800‑GOT‑JUNK passes this cost to the customer if your couch includes a mattress. 
* **Licensing & insurance** – All crews are fully licensed and insured, which is included in the quoted price. 

--- 

## When a Solo Couch Pickup Makes Sense (and When It Doesn’t) 

### Adding the Couch to a Larger Load 

If you have other junk (boxes, old appliances, yard waste), combine them into one volume load. The **average job across all customers is about $240**, which is often cheaper than paying two separate minimum‑load fees. 

**Example:** 

* Couch alone (high‑end estimate) = **$170** 
* Additional trash that fills the rest of a 1/8‑truck = $30 (average load factor) 
* **Combined total** = **$200** (still under two separate minimum loads of $100 + $100 = $200, but you avoid the second dispatch fee). 

### Worked Dollar Example 

You live in a mid‑west suburb where the on‑site estimate for a three‑seat sofa is **$120**. You also have a broken refrigerator ($115) and a pile of cardboard boxes that would fill the remaining space in a 1/8‑truck.

| Item | Individual price (if booked alone) | Combined price in one 1/8‑truck |
|------|------------------------------------|---------------------------------|
| Sofa | $120 | — |
| Refrigerator | $115 | — |
| Cardboard (fills remaining space) | $30 (average) | — |
| **Total if separate** | **$265** | **$150** (single 1/8‑truck estimate) |

**Savings:** $265 − $150 = **$115** by consolidating into one pickup.

### When a Solo Pickup Is Worth It 

* You need the couch removed **today** and have no other junk. 
* Your couch is the only item that fits the **minimum‑load** space, so the crew can charge the low end of the single‑item range. 
* You live in a high‑cost market where the volume surcharge would push a half‑truck load above $600; a solo quote of $150‑$170 may be cheaper.

--- 

## Preparing Your Couch for Removal 

### Disassembly, Clearance, Pathway 

1. **Remove legs or detachable sections** – many couches have removable legs that reduce volume. 
2. **Clear a 3‑foot path** from the couch to the driveway or loading zone. 
3. **Take out cushions** if they are separate; they count as additional volume but are lighter. 

### Documentation for Estimate 

* Have the **couch’s dimensions** (length, width, height) and **weight** (if known). 
* Note any **special handling** (e.g., a built‑in recliner mechanism). 
* Provide **photos** if you’re booking online; the crew will still verify on site, but photos speed up the estimate. 

--- 

## Alternatives to 1‑800‑GOT‑JUNK 

### Municipal Bulk Pickup 

Many cities offer **free or low‑cost bulk pickup** (often $0‑$50). Limits usually include a weight cap (e.g., 200 lb) and a schedule (once per month). Check your local public works website for exact rules.

### Retailer Haul‑Away 

If you’re buying a new sofa, most big‑box retailers (IKEA, Costco, Ashley) provide **free haul‑away** for the old item when you schedule delivery. The service is limited to one item per delivery and may require the couch to be near the door.

### Donation or Resale 

* **Charities** (Goodwill, Habitat for Humanity) often pick up furniture for free, but they may reject items with stains, damage, or excessive weight. 
* **Online marketplaces** (Craigslist, Facebook Marketplace) let you sell or give away the couch; you handle the loading yourself.

### DIY & Flex Service 

1‑800‑GOT‑JUNK’s **Flex** product lets you **load the couch into a bag or container yourself** and pay a flat **$39** collection fee. This works only if the couch can be broken down to fit a standard 55‑gal trash bag or a small container, which is rare but possible for loveseats.

--- 

### Cost Comparison Table 

| Provider | Pricing Model | Minimum Charge | Typical Couch Cost* | Notes |
|----------|---------------|----------------|---------------------|-------|
| **1‑800‑GOT‑JUNK** | Volume + single‑item | $100‑$150 (1/8‑truck) | **$59‑$170** | On‑site estimate; includes labor, haul, disposal |
| **LoadUp** | Per‑item, guaranteed online | $89 | $89‑$119 (average) | Fixed price, no surprise fees |
| **Junk King** | Volume | $99 | $99‑$149 (estimated) | Half‑truck $389‑$488; online estimate only |
| **College Hunks** | Volume + $99 dispatch fee | $150 | $150‑$250 | Dispatch fee often hidden until booking |
| **Municipal bulk** | Fee per load | $0‑$50 | $0‑$50 (if eligible) | Limits on weight/size; schedule constraints |
| **Retailer haul‑away** | Free with purchase | $0 | $0 (if buying new) | Only one item per delivery; may require curbside placement |

\*Ranges reflect the verified $59‑$170 couch range plus typical volume adjustments.

--- 

## Common Mistakes People Make 

| Mistake | Why It Costs More | How to Avoid |
|---------|-------------------|--------------|
| **Assuming the advertised “minimum load” price applies to a single couch** | The minimum load is a **truck volume** price; a heavy couch may exceed the 1/8‑truck space, triggering a higher tier. | Ask the crew to measure the couch on‑site; consider adding other junk to fill the load. |
| **Leaving the couch on the curb** | Some junk‑removal firms charge extra for curb‑side loading; 1‑800‑GOT‑JUNK does not, but other companies do. | Keep the couch inside or at the door; the crew will come to you. |
| **Not checking for local recycling fees** | In CA, CT, RI a $10.50 mattress fee can appear unexpectedly. | Verify if your couch includes a mattress; ask about the fee during the estimate. |
| **Booking a “same‑day” service without confirming availability** | Same‑day slots are limited; last‑minute bookings may incur a premium or be denied. | Schedule at least 24‑48 hours in advance; be flexible on day/time. |
| **Using expired coupon codes** | Many aggregator sites list codes that no longer work, leading to frustration. | Sign up for the company’s email list for verified $10‑$25 discounts; watch for local franchise promos. |

--- 

## Frequently Asked Questions 

**Q1. How long does a couch removal take?** 
A typical 1‑800‑GOT‑JUNK crew loads a couch in 10‑15 minutes. Including travel and paperwork, the whole job usually finishes within an hour. 

**Q2. Do I need to move the couch to the curb?** 
No. The crew loads the couch from wherever it sits on your property—basement, garage, or living room. 

**Q3. What if my couch is larger than a half‑truck?** 
Couches rarely exceed a half‑truck (5 ft × 5 ft × 8 ft). If yours does, the crew will quote a **full‑truck** rate ($600‑$1,099). Consider disassembling or donating instead. 

**Q4. Is there a disposal fee for the couch?** 
All disposal fees are included in the quoted price. Only a separate mattress recycling fee applies in CA, CT, and RI. 

**Q5. Can I get a discount for being a veteran or senior?** 
There is **no official military, senior, student, or AAA discount**. The only reliable savings are email‑list coupons ($10‑$25) or local franchise promotions. 

**Q6. What if I need the couch removed today?** 
Same‑day service is often available but not guaranteed. Call the local franchise early in the day; flexibility on timing increases the chance of a same‑day slot. 

--- 

## Bottom‑Line Takeaway 

If you need **just one couch removed**, expect a price **between $59 and $170** after the free on‑site estimate. The cost can drop dramatically when you bundle the couch with other junk or share a truck with a neighbor. Always verify local fees (especially the $10.50 mattress fee in three states) and avoid expired coupon codes. When the price seems high, compare municipal bulk pickup, retailer haul‑away, or donation—often those free or low‑cost options beat a solo professional pickup.
